name: autogen

facts.description: A programming framework for agentic AI

title: AutoGen: A Programming Framework for Agentic AI
answer: AutoGen is Microsoft's open source Python framework for building multi-agent AI systems, where LLM-powered agents converse and collaborate to solve tasks. It sits above model APIs, handling orchestration, tool use, and inference tuning. The one thing to know before adopting it: version 0.4 is a significant rewrite with a migration guide, so new projects should start there while existing 0.2 code needs planned migration.

sections.body: AutoGen is a programming framework for agentic AI, created by Microsoft and hosted at github.com/microsoft/autogen under a CC-BY-4.0 licence. It is written in Python and first appeared in 2023, with version 0.4 released later and a migration guide published for earlier users. It occupies the orchestration layer of the AI stack: above raw model APIs and below full applications. Rather than calling a model once, AutoGen lets you define agents that hold conversations, call tools, and coordinate with each other, so the framework manages the back and forth that turns a language model into a working system.
sections.heading: What it is and where it sits in AI work

sections.body: The official site shows AutoGen used for multi-agent conversation, code generation and execution, mathematical problem solving through patterns such as MathChat, and defense against jailbreak attacks through the AutoDefense research framework. It also provides enhanced inference for OpenAI-compatible models, with caching, error handling, multi-config inference, result filtering, and templating. It is strongest when a task benefits from several specialized agents, for example an analyzer, a judge, and a coordinator, each with its own system prompt. The site also documents local model use through FastChat and ChatGLM, so it is not tied to one vendor.
sections.heading: What it is used for and where it is strongest

sections.body: AutoGen assumes working Python knowledge and familiarity with calling language model APIs. The documentation covers configuration through llm_config, config_list, tags, and JSON files, and it explains inference hyperparameters such as temperature, top_p, max_tokens, and n. Some concepts, like deepcopy behaviour in configuration objects and the retry order across models, require careful reading. The official site offers quickstart material, use case pages, and blog posts, but it does not present a structured beginner course, so a student should be comfortable reading reference documentation and experimenting with small examples before building anything substantial.
sections.heading: How hard it is to learn and what you need first

sections.body: AutoGen has a large community, with more than sixty one thousand stars on GitHub and an active repository last updated in April 2026. The official site states it is the official project and is not affiliated with any forks or startups. It integrates with AgentOps as its official agent observability tool, covering LLM calls, costs, latency, failures, multi-agent interactions, and tool usage from one dashboard. It works with OpenAI and Azure OpenAI endpoints, custom endpoints, and local models served through FastChat. Documentation includes a migration guide for version 0.4, blog posts, and research write-ups.
sections.heading: Ecosystem and community

sections.body: AutoGen supports both quick experiments and production use, though the balance differs by version. A few lines can start a conversation between agents, and the enhanced inference layer adds caching, error handling, and multi-config fallback that matter in production. The site presents AgentOps monitoring and logging as the way enterprises can trust AutoGen in production. The cost is conceptual overhead: configuration, model selection order, and agent coordination must be understood before behaviour is predictable. The site does not publish benchmark comparisons of latency or memory against other frameworks, so performance claims should be tested in your own setting.
sections.heading: Prototyping speed against production performance

sections.body: AutoGen is a current standard for multi-agent orchestration rather than a legacy choice, backed by Microsoft and used in published research such as AutoDefense. The site notes that Bloomberg declared 2024 the year of AI agents, and AutoGen positions itself around that trend. Its integration with AgentOps signals enterprise interest in observability and compliance. For someone choosing what to learn, AutoGen is a reasonable investment because agent orchestration skills transfer across frameworks, but the site does not list specific employers or job titles, so career claims beyond general demand for agent developers are not supported here.
sections.heading: Industry adoption and careers

sections.body: AutoGen is a Python framework, so it is typically used with the Python data and machine learning stack, and its inference layer wraps OpenAI-compatible APIs including openai-python. It can call local models through FastChat, which exposes OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and it has been used with ChatGLM and LLaMA-family models. In a polyglot pattern, AutoGen usually handles agent orchestration and tool calling while other services handle data processing, model serving, or user interfaces. The site does not document first-class bindings for other languages, so teams outside Python would need to call it as a service.
sections.heading: How it fits beside the others

sections.body: AutoGen is not a model training framework, and the site does not present it as one. Its documentation is split between 0.2 and 0.4, which can confuse readers, and the migration guide exists precisely because the API changed. The site does not publish systematic performance benchmarks, security guarantees, or a formal support policy. Observability depends on a third-party tool, AgentOps, rather than a built-in solution. Some research examples, such as AutoDefense, are experiments rather than products. Questions about long-term API stability, cost at scale, and behaviour under failure are not settled by the official material.
sections.heading: Limits and open questions
